Those newsletter tracking bits tacked onto the end of a link, and the little jump-to-a-section marker, don't change what the page actually *is* — it's the same article I already saved. So I wouldn't want a second, nearly-identical copy cluttering my library just because the address had some extra tail on it. Recognizing it as the same thing, quietly ignoring that noise, and taking me back to the clean bookmark I already have is exactly right — it's the same "don't make me duplicates, just take me to the one I've got" spirit from before, applied sensibly to these messy real-world links.
